title: Kestrel and the Oath
premise: Marguerite Ravensworth keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in stolen memories, bottled oaths, and other impossible things—until a royal edict declares all memory-thieves traitors and sends hunters into the city. Forced to flee, she discovers her own gift is rarer than she knew: she can restore memories, not just take them, making her the living key to an ancient covenant between the human realm and the fading Kestrel Court. Hunted by the crown's Inquisitor and betrayed by the guildmaster who raised her, Marguerite gathers a found family of outcasts to reforge the broken oath at the Standing Stones before the veil seals forever. She succeeds at terrible cost—sacrificing her own collected memories of the people she loves—and chooses to rebuild those bonds from nothing, proving that family is made by choice, not recollection.
about_author: Oscar Kavanagh is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forgotten letters and now writes fantasy about the things people refuse to remember. They live in a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, and they insist this is not suspicious.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Thefts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She audits the guild's ledgers by candlelight, cataloguing traded memories while slipping a stolen lullaby back to a grieving widow for free. Establishes her quiet rebellion and loneliness. Emotional beat: tenderness hidden inside routine.

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The royal herald nails the Proclamation of Severance to the guildhouse door: all memory-gifted are traitors. Guildmaster Corvane burns incriminating pages—and orders Marguerite to erase a client's memory as proof of loyalty. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The widow from chapter one is arrested; her recovered lullaby was traced. Marguerite realizes her mercy left evidence. She flees the guildhouse through the rooftops with only the oldest ledger. Beat: guilt and the end of invisibility.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Sold His Name
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. A street thief named Tobias catches Marguerite hiding and offers sanctuary in exchange for one memory: his own, which he sold years ago and wants back. Their wary bargain begins the found family. Beat: two lonely people negotiating trust.

chapters.title: Hollow Bells
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Inquisitor Seraphine Vale interrogates the widow publicly, using extracted memories as weapons. Marguerite watches from the crowd, recognizing Vale's gift—she steals without consent, leaving husks. Beat: horror at what her gift could become.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Doors
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. They seek Odile, an exiled mapmaker who charts passages between realms. Odile reveals the covenant of the Kestrel Court and that the veil thins each equinox. Beat: wonder—the story widens beyond survival into purpose.

chapters.title: A Memory That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Restoring Tobias's name-memory, Marguerite glimpses something impossible inside it: a fragment of the original covenant oath, spoken in a voice like wind through feathers. Beat: revelation that her gift is restoration, not theft.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The guildmaster, revealed as a former covenant-keeper who broke his oath decades ago, offers Marguerite amnesty if she surrenders the ledger and her gift. His chapters expose his fear disguised as pragmatism. Beat: betrayal wearing a father's face.

chapters.title: Feathers in the Snow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Ambushed by Vale's hunters, Marguerite is saved by Wren—a knight of the Kestrel Court, half-faded, bound to find an oathbearer. Wren confirms Marguerite is the last one. Beat: awe and the weight of destiny arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: The Road Under the River
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. The company travels Odile's hidden road beneath the frozen river; Tobias nearly drowns saving the ledger, and Marguerite realizes she loves him. Quiet campfire scene, shared stories. Beat: love kindling against duty's cold.

chapters.title: Vale's Empty Room
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. We enter the Inquisitor's mind: every memory she has taken sits in her like stones, including one she cannot place—an oath she witnessed as a child. Beat: the antagonist revealed as another victim of the broken covenant.

chapters.title: The Guildhouse Burns
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Returning for Odile's stolen maps, they find Corvane has sold the guild's secrets to the crown; the guildhouse burns with the archive inside. Marguerite saves one child apprentice, Nettie. Beat: rage, loss, and the family growing anyway.

chapters.title: What Corvane Broke
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Flashback interlude: forty years ago, young Corvane refused to pay the covenant's price—giving up his dearest memory—and fled, dooming the realms to slow decay. Beat: tragic understanding of how duty curdles into cowardice.

chapters.title: The Price on the Stone
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the Standing Stones, Wren explains the reforging requires an oathbearer to surrender their most treasured memories willingly. Marguerite hides that hers are all of Tobias, Odile, Nettie—the family she just found. Beat: dread settling over devotion.

chapters.title: Nettie's Question
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Young Nettie asks whether forgetting someone means they stop mattering. Marguerite cannot answer honestly and lies badly. Tobias overhears enough to suspect the truth. Beat: the cost made intimate and unbearable.

chapters.title: Seraphine Turns
chapters.summary: Seraphine's POV. Ordered to execute captured memory-gifted children, Vale instead releases them, haunted by the oath-fragment in her own stolen hoard. She defects toward the Stones, hunted by her own soldiers. Beat: antagonist becoming ally.

chapters.title: The Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. The company converges on the Stones as the veil tears; Corvane arrives with crown troops, offering Marguerite one last chance to walk away whole. She refuses. Battle ignites among the monoliths. Beat: everything staked at once.

chapters.title: Kestrel and the Oath
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax. Amid the battle, Marguerite speaks the covenant and pays its price: her memories of her found family dissolve as the veil mends and the Kestrel Court breathes again. Tobias reaches her too late. Beat: sacrifice fulfilled in devastating silence.

chapters.title: Strangers at a Fire
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Aftermath: the realm steadies, but Marguerite wakes knowing no one's name. Tobias introduces himself as if for the first time, heartbroken and determined. Beat: grief transformed into a choice to begin again.

chapters.title: The Ledger Reopened
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She reopens the guild under new law, restoring rather than stealing, with Vale as reluctant protector and Odile charting legal crossings. Fragments of feeling persist—she cries at a lullaby she doesn't recognize. Beat: hope threaded through absence.

chapters.title: What Remains When Memory Fails
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Over seasons, Tobias retells their story to Marguerite nightly, refusing to let the record die. Slowly she falls for him again—not remembering, but choosing. Beat: love against duty resolved as love beyond memory.

chapters.title: First Entry, New Hand
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Final chapter: Marguerite writes the first line of a new ledger—'We were strangers once'—and smiles at Tobias across the room, certain of him without knowing why. The covenant holds; the family holds. Beat: belonging earned, not remembered.
